question: What is the atomicity of Phosphorous?
solution:
The correct answer is "**Tetra-Atomic**".

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__ **

__
 
• Tetra atomic molecules are those **molecules which are formed by combination of four atoms like NH3**.
 
• Tetra atomic ions are charged species that contain four covalently linked atoms.
 
• Tetra atomic ions are a type of **polyatomic ions**.
 
• Examples of tetra atomic ions are,**H3O+( 3 atoms of H + 1 atom of O), SO32-, NO3-**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The prefix poly- means many, so a polyatomic ion is an ion that contains **more than one atom****.**
 
• This differentiates polyatomic ions from monatomic ions, which contain only one atom.
 
• "Monatomic" is a combination of the words "**mono**" and "**atomic**", and means "**single atom**".
 
• It is usually applied to gases: a monatomic gas is one gas in which atoms are not bound to each other.
 
• Diatomic molecules are molecules composed of only two atoms, of the same or different chemical elements.
 
• If a diatomic molecule consists of two atoms of the same element, such as hydrogen or oxygen, then it is said to be **homonuclear**.
